html:
The Dominican Republic is the country on the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola, independent since 1844.

Its capital, Santo Domingo, was the first lasting European city in the Americas, founded by Spain in the 1490s on land of the Taíno, who were almost wiped out within a few decades. The colony then sank into poverty while French Haiti next door grew rich. Spain ceded it to France in 1795, and from 1822 to 1844 Haiti ruled the whole island.

A secret society led by Juan Pablo Duarte declared independence from Haiti on 27 February 1844. The new state was unstable:

  • In 1861 its president handed it back to Spain; the Restoration War won it back by 1865.
  • The United States took control of its customs in 1905 and occupied the country from 1916 to 1924.
  • Rafael Trujillo ruled as dictator from 1930 until he was shot in 1961. In 1937 his troops killed thousands of Haitians in the Parsley massacre.
  • After a civil war in 1965, US troops landed again, and Joaquín Balaguer, Trujillo's old aide, ruled for most of the next three decades.

Since the 1990s the country has held regular elections and grown fast on tourism and trade. It is known for merengue and for producing many of the best baseball players in the United States.
sum: The Dominican Republic is the country on the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola, independent since 1844.
